--- title: "Overview and workflow" subtitle: "The typed path from dataset to first-level fit, contrast, and group summary." jupyter: python3 execute: freeze: auto --- ## The Workflow `fmrimod` runs one typed workflow from data to group results. Every arrow below is a typed Python value, not a string or a hand-built matrix: ```text fmri_dataset -> fmri_lm(spec) -> contrast -> group ``` This page walks the first-level segment on a small example with a known injected effect; the [golden path](golden-path.qmd) carries the same workflow all the way into the group stage. ## Dataset An event table plus an acquisition grid, bound together in an `fmri_dataset`. ::: {#482523ea .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd import fmrimod as fm from fmrimod.spec import hrf from fmrimod.contrast import condition events = pd.DataFrame({ "onset": np.arange(8, 210, 12.0), "stim_type": np.where(np.arange(17) % 2 == 0, "face", "scene"), "duration": 2.0, }) ``` ::: We use simulated data with a **known** face−scene effect of `2.0` in five of ten voxels. The point of working with simulated data here is that we know the right answer: a correct fit must return ≈ `2.0` in those voxels and ≈ `0` in the other five. ::: {#c88bb7ab .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} spec = hrf("stim_type", basis="spmg1") ``` ::: `dataset_with_effect` is a tutorial helper that builds the simulated data with the known effect placed on the `condition("face", ...)` column — the same object the contrast below tests, so what we inject and what we measure are the same condition by construction. ::: {#ddb9a239 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} from fmrimod.simulate.demo import dataset_with_effect sampling = fm.SamplingFrame(blocklens=220, TR=1.0) dataset = dataset_with_effect( spec, events, on=condition("face", term="stim_type"), effect=2.0, sampling_frame=sampling, seed=42, ) ``` ::: ## Typed Spec → First-Level Fit The spec is a typed `hrf(...)` value — one HRF-convolved regressor per stimulus level. `fmri_lm` compiles it, adds the baseline, and returns an inspectable fit. ::: {#a2c818fe .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit = fm.fmri_lm(spec, dataset) fit # typed FmriLmResult — coefficients, residual df, solver config ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` FmriLm( n_coefficients=3, n_voxels=10, residual_df=217.0, config=FmriLmConfig(OLS), contrasts=[], ) ``` ::: ::: The realized design is readable from the fit — built for you, still inspectable. ::: {#ff260319 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} list(fit.model.design_matrix(run=0).columns) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` ['stim_type_stim_type.face', 'stim_type_stim_type.scene', 'base_constant1_block_1'] ``` ::: ::: ## Typed Contrast The scientific comparison names conditions, not column positions. ::: {#557bca96 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} face_vs_scene = fit.contrast( condition("face", term="stim_type") - condition("scene", term="stim_type"), name="face_vs_scene", ) pd.DataFrame({ "estimate": face_vs_scene.estimate.round(3), "t": face_vs_scene.stat.round(2), "p": face_vs_scene.p_value.round(4), }) # voxels 0–4 recover the injected ≈ 2.0; voxels 5–9 are null ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
estimate t p
0 1.023 1.08 0.2815
1 2.011 2.13 0.0347
2 3.091 3.30 0.0011
3 1.734 1.68 0.0936
4 1.178 1.29 0.1970
5 0.679 0.71 0.4796
6 0.975 0.94 0.3486
7 0.967 0.99 0.3241
8 0.360 0.36 0.7199
9 -0.893 -0.88 0.3797
``` ::: ::: The estimate returns the effect we injected. Recovering the planted value (not just *some* value) is the evidence that the design, the fit, and the contrast weights are all specified correctly. ## The Final Stage The final arrow — carrying these per-subject `ContrastResult` objects into a second-level (group) model to ask whether the effect holds across subjects — is shown end to end, with a check against Nilearn, on the **[golden path](golden-path.qmd)**. We stop at the first level here so each stage stays small enough to read; the golden path is the same workflow run without a break. ## Where to go next The same dataset-and-spec pattern carries through to the rest of the modeling stack: alternative GLM engines, AR whitening for temporally correlated noise, single-trial estimation, and ready-made benchmark datasets. Each is one option on the same `fmri_lm` call rather than a separate API to learn. ## Next - [The golden path](golden-path.qmd) — the whole workflow into group, with a parity check - [Linear model](linear-model.qmd) - [Contrasts](contrasts.qmd) - [Group analysis](group-analysis.qmd)
